Context: This text describes a meeting between Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville and the Natchez tribe. It was most likely written by someone traveling with d'Iberville.
Title: Source 2: Adapted from Historical Journal (1699)
Content: When we arrived near the Natchez village, the ambassador¹ sang several songs of peace, accompanied by loud yells. The Indians gathered on the bank of the river, where they had cut the cane away to receive us. The chief was surrounded by about `text(sixty)` persons. D'Iberville was greeted by them in the usual manner. They began by raising their arms towards the sun, as in respect, then passed their hands over his chest, which is a curious form of affection² among them. They then brought us Indian corn. D'Iberville then handed out beads, needles, looking-glasses, knives, and other gifts.
References: ambassador: a person who represents a group
